newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Tuesday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were narrowly mixed. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.65/2.60 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.60/2.55 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.65/2.55 percent against 2.61/2.56 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.72/98.77 from Monday's close of S$98.63/98.68, May 2002 at S$99.52/99.57 versus S$99.53/99.58 and June 2003 at S$94.62/94.67 against S$94.58//94.63.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 4 3-7/8 percent from Monday's 4-1/4 4 percent.
